set_aside.subject: K-02 purity and admission
set_aside.text: A flow is a small proven graph of two kinds of node: a pure function an agent wrote ... Every promise ... is a promise about code whose outputs depend only on its inputs; the kernel neither checks that
set_aside.question: What makes an admitted implementation a "pure function," and what observable result or failure occurs when code depends on an undeclared process fact?
options: Purity is only an author obligation; conforming trial outputs permit admission and later differing outputs are ordinary results
Purity is an admission condition enforced by some named check or evidence
Such code may run but the implementation, verdict or execution is explicitly marked as having no purity guarantee
set_aside.default_guess: Treat purity as an unenforced author obligation and admit solely from the recorded trial results.

witness.initial: A contract has a trial case, and an implementation reads an ambient process value that is stable during admission but later changes.
events: The kernel tries it and records a passing verdict.
An owner or agent runs the same function with the same declared input after the ambient value changes.
outcomes: The node is a pure function and must return the admitted result because equal declared inputs require equal outputs.
The node returns a different result because the kernel admitted it from its trial outputs and does not check dependence on process facts.
witness.observer: The owner or agent reading the run output and trace.

set_aside.subject: K-02 function inputs and outputs
set_aside.text: code whose outputs depend only on its inputs
set_aside.question: For this promise, what exactly counts as an input, what counts as an output, and within what identity scope must equality hold?
options: Inputs are only declared port values and outputs are only declared port values, per implementation version
Inputs also include execution-visible file names or metadata, contract/resource settings, or other invocation context
Outputs include failures, timeouts, resource observations and trace status as well as declared values
The promise compares executions only within one implementation activation, or instead across implementations of the same contract
set_aside.default_guess: Compare declared output values for equal declared input values within one immutable implementation version; do not include trace timing or resource observations.

witness.initial: The same immutable implementation is invoked twice with identical file content, but the kernel supplies different spool paths and the second execution experiences different scheduling.
events: The implementation derives a declared result from the input file path or times out under the second schedule.
An agent runs the flow twice with the same logical file value.
outcomes: The executions had equal inputs, so the changed result or success status violates the promise.
The path or execution context was an input, or the timeout was not an output, so the promise is not violated.
witness.observer: The agent comparing the two run traces and results.

set_aside.subject: K-02 sandbox process boundary
set_aside.text: the kernel neither checks that nor masks any other fact of the process
set_aside.question: Which concrete process facts are visible to function code, and which component establishes them, given that later implementations must construct the sandbox consistently from this text alone?
options: A named minimal set of Python and operating-system facts is visible
All non-secret facts inherited by the sandbox process, such as environment, locale, working directory, process identifiers and platform details, are visible
Each sandbox implementation may expose whatever non-secret ambient facts its runtime naturally supplies
set_aside.default_guess: Expose only the ordinary facts of a freshly created isolated sandbox process after removing credentials and service handles, accepting that their exact values may vary.

witness.initial: An installation has a non-secret environment value and host locale; neither is a declared function input.
events: An agent submits Python code that reads the environment value or locale through the standard library.
The implementation is executed in a disposable sandbox.
outcomes: The sandbox inherits the fact because the kernel masks no other process fact, and the code can return it.
The sandbox starts with a minimal constructed environment, so the fact is absent even though it exists in the kernel or host process.
witness.observer: The agent receiving the trial evidence or flow output.

set_aside.subject: K-02 ambient facts and K-14 disclosure
set_aside.text: the kernel neither checks that nor masks any other fact of the process
set_aside.question: What disclosure class and port-validation rule applies when a function output derives from a process fact that did not arrive through a declared, classified input port?
options: Every visible process fact is guaranteed open
Process facts receive declared disclosure classes and count among the values the execution received
Functions may expose non-secret process facts without classification
All ambient-derived output is conservatively assigned a specified class
set_aside.default_guess: Require every sandbox-visible ambient fact to be non-sensitive and treat it as open.

witness.initial: A sandbox-visible, non-credential environment value contains business-confidential installation information; the function's only declared input is open.
events: An agent submits a function that includes the environment value in its output.
The function passes its trial and runs in a flow.
outcomes: K-14 assigns the output the highest class of the declared input, open, so the agent receives the value.
The ambient fact must contribute its own class or be withheld, so the agent does not receive it as open.
witness.observer: The agent and the owner auditing the disclosure.
